title: Keeping everyone standing through a run
target: How to use health packs, the truck's healer and the revive item in R.E.P.O. so that a bad moment costs the crew a detour rather than the run.
version: 0.4.0, read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A crew of two or more
At least one health pack bought

steps.do: Watch the health readout rather than counting hits, because health is a tracked number with a display of its own.
steps.because: a player's health is tracked and shown in its own interface (PlayerHealth, HealthUI)

steps.do: Carry a health pack before you need one, because recovery uses a carried pack rather than a command.
steps.because: recovery uses a carried health pack (ItemHealthPack)

steps.do: Treat the truck as a healer and not only as the way out, because it has a healer of its own.
steps.because: the truck has a healer of its own rather than only a drop-off point (TruckHealer)

steps.do: Do not count on every heal working, because the game has effects for a full heal and a separate one for a heal that failed.
steps.because: healing has its own effects, including one for a failed heal (fullHealParticle, fullHealSmokeParticle, failedHealParticles)

steps.do: Keep an eye on how many packs are around, since the game works out how many are available and keeps a count.
steps.because: the game works out how many health packs are available and keeps an amount (potentialItemHealthPacks, itemHealthPacksAmount)

steps.do: Decide when to stop hitting a monster by its health rather than by its looks, because it has a health total and a freeze time for dying.
steps.because: a monster carries a health total and a freeze time for dying (EnemyHealth, deathFreezeTime)

steps.do: Use weight deliberately, because a light, a medium and a heavy impact each do their own damage.
steps.because: impacts hurt a monster with separate damage for light, medium and heavy (impactHurt, impactLightDamage, impactMediumDamage, impactHeavyDamage)

steps.do: Remember that a kill can leave something behind, because a monster can be set to spawn a valuable up to a maximum.
steps.because: it can be set to leave a valuable behind up to a maximum number (spawnValuable, spawnValuableMax)

steps.do: Revive with the carried device rather than looking for a button: it is an item, and it shows what it is doing.
steps.because: reviving is done with a carried item that has lights, lines, particles and a shockwave (ItemReviveItem, lineRendererL, lineRendererR, shockwavePrefab)

steps.do: Spend upgrade money on health and stamina as a plan rather than a repair, because both are upgrades of their own.
steps.because: health and stamina can both be upgraded, each with its own wording (playerUpgradeHealth, playerUpgradeStamina, localizedUpgradeHealth, localizedUpgradeStamina)

commonMistakes: Leaving the health packs in the truck and meeting the first real monster without one.
Assuming a heal always lands, when a failed heal is a thing the game draws and plays.
Hitting a monster until it looks dead instead of reading its health and its dying freeze.
Treating reviving as a command and forgetting the device has to be carried and aimed.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. The grounding for each step is listed on the technical reference pages; nothing here is estimated.
